Hi Evelyn,

Thanks for sending the order form. Procurement had a quick pass and we have a handful of commercial clarifications before we route to Finance for PO issuance:

- Tax treatment: can Redwood confirm which entity will invoice FinApps and whether Redwood will gross-up for VAT/GST or if FinApps will be responsible for taxes?
- Minimum commitment: procurement wants the minimum commit to be presented as an annual committed spend that can be pro-rated if the contract starts part-way through the year.
- Net terms: FinApps normally requires Net 30; your draft shows Net 45. Is Net 30 possible or can we agree on Net 45 with early-pay discounts?
- Invoicing cadence: they prefer quarterly invoices with the ability to split between product lines. Will Redwood accept split invoices to match our internal chargebacks?
- PO details: we'll need a format for PO number and billing address to include on the invoice.

I've attached our procurement redlines (OrderForm_v2_redlines.pdf) and a tax residency certificate for the EU entity. Can we get a short written response to each of the points above before we schedule signature? If helpful, happy to do a 30-minute call.

Hi Sanjay — appreciate the clear list. Short answers up front and then next steps below so you can share with Finance: 

1) Tax responsibility: FinApps will be responsible for VAT/GST where applicable; Redwood will issue invoices from Redwood, Inc. (US) for this deal. We will provide the tax documentation you need (tax residency certificate, VAT invoice) and will cooperate on any required filings. If the transaction is taxable in your jurisdiction, FinApps will remit tax; Redwood does not generally gross-up.

2) Minimum commit: We can present the minimum as an annual committed spend and include pro-ration language for mid-year starts. We'll mark that in the order form and show an annualized schedule in the commercial table.

3) Net terms: Our standard for enterprise agreements is Net 45. We can consider Net 30 for strategic customers but that requires Finance approval (and may impact pricing / credit profile). Alternatively we can offer a 2% 10-day early-pay discount.

4) Invoicing cadence: Quarterly invoicing with split lines per product is OK — we can break invoices by product code/usage bucket. Please confirm whether you need separate invoices to different cost centers or a single invoice with line-level allocation.

5) PO requirements: Send PO number + billing address and we will mirror those fields on the invoice. We also accept an emailed PO or standard SOW/PO combo.

Next steps:
- I've updated the commercial tab and prepared an OrderForm_v3 that incorporates the annualized minimum and a proposed quarterly invoice schedule (attached).
- Karthik will provide suggested contract redlines for the tax and payment sections for your legal team to consider.
- If Net 30 is a hard requirement, please let me know and I'll escalate to Finance for a credit review.

If you want a 30-minute call to walk through the table, I can do tomorrow morning. Otherwise please confirm the PO format and whether Net 45 is acceptable as next steps.

Best,

- Tax gross-up: FinApps' legal prefers an explicit clause that taxes are the customer's responsibility (including VAT) and that Redwood will not gross-up. Can Redwood add a sentence confirming that Redwood will provide supporting VAT invoices where required?
- Annualized minimum: confirm that pro-ration will be straight-line based on service start date (FinApps to avoid step functions).
- Net terms: FinApps has a hard procurement requirement of Net 30. If Finance rejects Net 30 we will likely have to re-evaluate the vendor selection. Is there any precedent for Net 30 for customers of your size?

Hi Sanjay — looping in from Legal/RevOps. Below are the edits we propose for the MSA / Order Form to cover the items you raised. I kept the language concise so it can be dropped into the redline PDF.

1) Taxes: "Customer shall bear all taxes, duties, or similar governmental assessments (except for Redwood's income taxes). Redwood will, upon request, provide VAT-compliant invoices and reasonable supporting documentation."

2) Gross-up: "Except as required by applicable law, Redwood shall not be required to gross-up any amounts payable under this Agreement for taxes."

3) Minimum Commit: "Minimum committed spend shall be stated as an annual amount. If the Service commences other than on the first day of the annual term, the minimum commitment shall be pro-rated on a straight-line basis for the portion of the year that the Service is active."

4) Net Terms & Early Payment: "Standard payment terms are Net 45. Customer may request Net 30, subject to Redwood's credit approval. Redwood may offer an early payment discount of 2% if payment is received within 10 days."

5) Invoicing & Split Invoices: "Redwood may issue multiple invoices per billing period at Customer's request. Customer must provide AP identifiers for each cost center; Redwood will either issue separate invoices per AP identifier or a single invoice with line-item mappings to each AP identifier as mutually agreed in writing."

6) PO Requirements: "Invoices shall reference Customer PO numbers; failure to include a PO does not relieve Customer's payment obligations provided Redwood subsequently receives a valid PO referencing the invoice."

I've implemented those redlines in OrderForm_v3_redlines.pdf (attached). If the Net 30 requirement is non-negotiable, please indicate and we'll run a quick Finance risk/credit check.

Evelyn — once Sanjay confirms acceptability of the language, I can prepare a clean version for DocuSign.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Legal Ops, Redwood Inference
